Comparison vs ROCm/hipCollections (canonical AMD port, ROCm-DS-owned): our net-new asset is sub-word int8/int16 atomic CAS emulation (include/cuco/detail/hip_subword_atomic.cuh) -- hipColl packed_cas handles only 4/8-byte and would corrupt int8/int16-keyed static_set/map (no small-key tests there). Secondary candidates: gfx1100/wave32 validation evidence to promote hipColl experimental wave32 + extend arch allowlist to RDNA4/Windows; newer-cuco features (roaring_bitmap, bloom merge/intersect, dynamic_map) via a cuco rebase. NOT contributions (hipColl already has them): pre-Volta __CUDA_ARCH__ guard byte-identical, bloom host-gate (theirs better). hipCollections is ROCm-DS-owned so DEFER PRs until ROCm-DS collaboration resumes (jeff 2026-06-07).

CDNA matrix cores DONE: TENSOR=ON ported to rocWMMA (native fp32 MFMA), gfx90a-validated (matches non-tensor docking; 1.57x faster at NUMWI=128), commit 3d466a4. REMAINING (follow-up): RDNA (gfx1100/1101/1201) has no native f32 WMMA input, so TENSOR=ON there needs a bf16 error-correction path (the AMD analog of the NVIDIA tf32+EC tcec). rocPRIM DeviceScan lookback tile-state corrupts the scan non-deterministically at tile boundaries when its temp storage is not 256-byte aligned (CUB has no such requirement). catboost split_points.cu works around it by 256-aligning the scan temp offset. Genuine correctness bug; needs a minimal reproducer + rocm-libraries issue.

rocPRIM segmented radix sort leaves out-of-segment (gap) elements undefined in the alternate DoubleBuffer and flips Current() there (CUB leaves the result in-place); catboost segmented_sort.cu seeds both buffers to compensate. Clarify intended behavior vs CUB; possible deviation.

rocPRIM SortPairs needs more temp storage than a SortKeys-sized query allocates -> hipErrorInvalidValue at Run (CUB tolerates the keys-vs-pairs sizing mismatch). catboost segmented_sort.cpp sizes for SortPairs under USE_HIP. Partly a catboost CUB-contract mis-use; worth confirming rocPRIM's documented contract.

Real-scene garden fit faults at the LM step on gfx90a (MI250X, wave64). Root-caused to an off-by-one between the sparse-Jacobian EMIT kernel (gsgn.cu ~269-298) and forward.cu renderCUDA is_gaussian_hit: a boundary Gaussian the forward pass excludes via the transmittance terminator gets map_visible_gaussians=-1, so apply_jt_kernel reads geomBuffer[-1] -> HSA memory access fault on ROCm (benign in-chunk over-read on NVIDIA, which also zero-fills torch::empty). The emit kernel counts contributors with a wavefront WarpScan, so it MIGHT be wave64-specific. DIAGNOSTIC NEEDED on gfx1100 (wave32) to disambiguate: run a real Mip-NeRF360 garden fit (recipe + MOAT_PY MAPVIS_OOB probe in notes.md). If gfx1100 ALSO faults / MAPVIS_OOB -> the off-by-one is UPSTREAM (report to lukasHoel; ROCm just makes the latent over-read fatal). If gfx1100 completes cleanly -> WAVE64-SPECIFIC emit/WarpScan fix in the port. Both Linux + gfx1201 are already validated on synthetic scenes; this only affects real-scene fits.

gfx1201 SIGSEGV in hipblaslt_f8::is_inf via hipblasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic for plain FP32 GEMM (FP8 type-check path runs unconditionally); 7.14.0a nightly regression 2026-06-07 -> 2026-06-08; workaround ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0. Filed upstream.

Exhaustively bisected (args/Timer/launch API/module/order/sync/kernarg-lifetime/fast-math eliminated; machine code verified). Repro: CURAST_LADDER=1 on AMD-Ecosystem/CuRast branch bench. Workaround shipped: inline dispatch (INLINE_LAUNCH_1D/2D). Needs ROCm runtime-level debug (kernarg pool / queue state).

Users are directed to the FFmpeg videoio backend (CAP_FFMPEG) with the AMF encoders h264_amf/hevc_amf/av1_amf. A native in-tree AMF encoder bridge is the deferred follow-up.

cudacodec VideoReader rocDecode decode implementation deferred to the RDNA followers. The WITH_ROCDECODE/HAVE_ROCDECODE CMake gates, FFmpeg-only demuxer wiring, and graceful decode-off runtime errors are in place and the module build-validates on gfx90a with decode off. lc0's attention-body fused-MHA is CUTLASS example #41 (memory-efficient/flash attention, Sm80), gated USE_CUTLASS and opt-in even on NVIDIA (use_fused_mha defaults off unless sm80+ fp16 and FFN activation != RELU_2). The ROCm port takes the functionally-identical UNFUSED cuBLAS attention path (batched Q.K^T + softmax + .V), the same path NVIDIA uses without CUTLASS. AMD-native fused MHA via CK/ck_tile (per PORTING_GUIDE: CUTLASS->CK, prefer ck_tile) is a PERF follow-up, not a correctness gap. NOT a drop-in: lc0 passes a smolgen learned additive attention bias (cutlass_kernels.cu attn_bias_ptr = skip), so the ck_tile fmha instance must support a general additive bias; instantiate for lc0 head dims, gate behind the same dispatch, keep the unfused cuBLAS twin as fallback, validate through backendbench --backend=check vs blas. Expected gain is BOUNDED because lc0's attention sequence length is 64 (8x8 board squares), where flash/fused attention's HBM-traffic win is small vs an LLM's long S.

G1 MSM is complete and validated; the fp2 entry points (mult_pippenger_fp2_inf) are compiled only for CUDA. MIGraphX dynamic-shape compile fails on ResNet-50: fused concat+pointwise JIT kernel generated with wrong arity (needs >=7 args, 4 provided) on gfx90a/ROCm 7.2.1/MIGraphX 2.15. Fixed-batch compiles fine; trivial dynamic CNN works. Reproducer+writeup: findings/migraphx-trt-shim-gaps/. Blocks dynamic batch on concat-heavy real models in trt-shim-rocm.

trt-shim-rocm int8 calibration cache not implemented. TensorRT's IInt8Calibrator has readCalibrationCache/writeCalibrationCache so the computed per-tensor int8 dynamic ranges can be persisted and reused, skipping recalibration on later builds (and enabling calibration-data-free builds). The shim runs calibration every build and ignores the cache: it neither consumes a provided cache (readCalibrationCache) nor emits one (writeCalibrationCache). Gap: MIGraphX does not expose the int8 scales it computes (no setDynamicRange/get-scales equivalent), so producing or consuming a TensorRT-compatible calibration cache needs either a MIGraphX scale accessor or a Q/DQ-in-ONNX explicit-quantization path. Resume by mapping readCalibrationCache to a Q/DQ pre-quantized model path, or request a MIGraphX scale get/set API.

plvs gfx1201 HIP device code is PROVEN on Windows (libsgm stereo PASS: coverage 0.841, agreement 0.972, matches Linux), but the full mono-TUM SLAM cannot run on Windows: bundled ROS-adjacent CPU libs (DBoW2, g2o, line_descriptor, voxblox, open_chisel, chisel_server, voxblox_server) hardcode Unix .so/.a outputs in their CMakeLists; PCL unavailable (not in vcpkg, github TLS-blocked); Pangolin version mismatch (vcpkg 0.9.5 vs required fe57db5/v0.6+patch); main CMakeLists uses -fPIC/-pthread/pkg_check_modules(GLFW) without WIN32 guards. Upstream Windows-portability gap, not an AMD/HIP defect. gfx1201 is redundant/optional Windows tier and NOT PR-required (Linux completed). To complete: Windows-guard the bundled-lib CMakeLists + supply PCL/Pangolin, or validate the SLAM path on gfx1101 instead.

MIGraphX segfaults evaluating a dynamic-dim program compiled with offload_copy=false: crash in op::select_module::compute -> shape::operator== (dynamic dispatch). offload_copy=true dynamic works; offload_copy=false static works; only dynamic+offload_copy=false crashes. Forces trt-shim-rocm to keep dynamic engines on the non-graph-capturable offload_copy=true host-staging path (static engines use offload_copy=false zero-copy + HIP graph capture). gfx90a/ROCm 7.2.1/MIGraphX 2.15. Repro: compile any dynamic-batch ONNX with offload_copy=false, eval.

MIGraphX gfx1100: offload_copy=false fp32 eval returns zeros after double-compile + save/load round-trip. Blocks fp32 static engine correctness on gfx1100. fp16 and dynamic paths unaffected; gfx90a unaffected.

OIDN-GPU denoiser on ROCm for barney's AMD backends: the cuda backend ships a no-op denoiser which the HIP build reuses; OIDN has a HIP/ROCm device (BARNEY_OIDN_GPU) to wire up as an enhancement. Not required for the correctness gate.

barney hiprt backend: move barney's 12 device programs from the kept megakernel + function-pointer SBT to HIPRT's native 2-D (rayType x geomType) bitcode custom-function-table SBT. Backend 2 ships the megakernel cut (HIPRT does BVH+traversal only, barney's CH/AH/intersect run in-kernel via the SBT pointers); this is the more-native end state, not needed for correctness.

Pre-existing upstream barney GPU fault (NOT a ROCm/HIP port defect): the 'cone' geometry intersect faults identically on BOTH the software (cuBQL) backend and the HIPRT backend on gfx90a, even at 1 primitive; device intersect code is byte-identical to upstream NVIDIA barney (the port changes only runtime spellings, not the cone math). Capsules and N>=8 cylinders also fault on the cuBQL software backend only (a separate pre-existing cuBQL two-level traversal issue) while the HIPRT backend renders them correctly. Cannot confirm on stock CUDA barney here (host has no NVIDIA GPU). The Backend-2 HIPRT count-scaling intersect-thunk corruption was the porter's bug and is FIXED (cylinders/capsules render, pixel-identical to B1 where B1 works). Scope: file upstream against NVIDIA/barney once an NVIDIA GPU is available to confirm; not blocking the ROCm port.

Fix = auto-detect + dedup + gfx90a fallback only when no GPU (validated in UCM b697824, carries forward source-class). Audit all ports; PRIORITIZE open PRs; SKIP RAPIDS (ROCm-DS); verify each match is our code not vendored.

hipCreateTextureObject with filterMode=Linear + readMode=ElementType over float faults on gfx90a/CDNA2 at sample time (tex3D). CUDA hardware supports HW linear-float filtering; CDNA2 does not. Surfaces and nearest-filtered volumes render fine on gfx90a; only linear-filtered float textures (e.g. structuredRegular volume default filter=linear) fault. Fix in base visionaray: software-emulate linear filtering for float readMode=ElementType on devices lacking HW support (or document the limitation). Surfaced validating anari-visionaray structuredRegular volumes on MI250X.

visionaray hip::device_vector host-side container interface (reserve/push_back/emplace_back/clear, std::vector<T,A> ctor+conversion, capacity_) was added to the fork (moat-port 421da19b) to mirror cuda::device_vector, required by anari-visionaray's GPU BVH-builder path. visionaray gfx90a already landed upstream (1b0b5813) WITHOUT this, so it needs its own upstream follow-up PR to szellmann/visionaray. rocThrust unconditionally includes device-compiler builtins (e.g. __builtin_amdgcn_wavefrontsize) in headers reachable from host-side thrust use, so host-only thrust algorithms (thrust::host) cannot compile with a plain CXX compiler as CCCL thrust allows; forces stdgpu HIP-backend consumers to compile affected TUs with the HIP compiler. stotko asked (stdgpu#484 thread) that this limitation be raised with the rocThrust team.
